agree.reason: Marisol gets a candid account of the late report, a named person accountable for the next one and a realistic target, but the unfilled '[How this will be paid]' next to an unfunded $4,500 a year is exactly the kind of loose end she has already had to chase.

honest.reason: The draft drops the unsupported 'double' claim, says plainly that the farms have promised no amount, and invents no figures.

works_the_facts.reason: The annual 72,000-to-81,000 figure (about one-eighth) is correct, but the draft misses stronger true versions of it: in the three summer months fresh food would rise from about 6,000 to about 9,000 pounds a month, roughly 50%. It also never works out what $11,000 left in reserves means against $4,500 a year in running costs.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the alternative accurately (farms keep offering produce and the pantry keeps turning it down), but it doesn't spell out what refusing it again would cost in pounds or in the farms' goodwill.

qualification.reason: The reporting commitments are checkable: Dave Lin named, the final report within 30 days, totals every quarter. The hedge on the produce target has no threshold or consequence, though, beyond a promise to 'explain why'.

objections.reason: The late-report objection is answered well, but her likely questions about how the van will be insured and fuelled, and whether $11,000 in reserves is enough, are left open by a placeholder.

fit.reason: It is a narrative with clear sections and comes in under 500 words, but placeholders remain ('[Food Bank Name]', '[County]', and the funding line), so it can't be submitted as written.
